content: In the context of disease prevention strategies, it is essential to focus on proper housing and husbandry practices for animals. Additionally, many countries may require technical and laboratory capacity-building support to effectively perform the recommended bacterial culture and sensitivity testing. International organizations, such as the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE), may provide assistance in implementing these guidelines. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) has emphasized the importance of countries conducting surveillance and monitoring of antimicrobial usage in food-producing animals. This is necessary to assess and evaluate the implementation of these guidelines effectively. The World Health Organization (WHO) will monitor research developments related to the use of antimicrobials in food-producing animals. WHO will also review and update these recommendations five years after the publication of the guidelines, unless significant new evidence emerges that warrants an earlier revision.
